Motion Studio · Issue #79

UI/UX Audit & Structural Overhaul Report

Unified single-bar product navigation, stage-first direct play across all four games, harmonized Motion Studio tokens across arcade and operator tools, and trimmed defensive captions—verified on real local Vite and production preview servers in English across desktop (1440×1000), mobile (390×844), and narrow (320×740) viewports.

What Changed & Why

1. Single Unified Product Bar

  • Replaced stacked double headers (117–220 px) with one 56–60 px Motion Studio bar in app-navigation.ts and studio-tokens.css.
  • Converted Switch view into an anchored floating popover with concise groups and zero multi-sentence prose walls.
  • Preserved all departure guards, NavigationStartup, motion-studio:navigation-check, Escape focus return, no-JS directory links, and hosted Pages route filtering.

2. Stage-First Direct Play

  • Removed the blocking modal curtain on load for Slap a Mole, Dodgeball, and Virtual Maze—players immediately see the game stage above the fold.
  • Added direct in-stage actions (Play without camera / Set up camera / Start round / Start rehearsal) and direct Play again through the existing clean reset/admission path.
  • Moved Motion Runner’s HUD into a top cabinet scoreboard bar so the 3D world and Start run sit cleanly above the fold on desktop and mobile.

3. Unified Visual Language & Bug Fixes

  • Created studio-tokens.css and harmonized Directory, Mole, Dodgeball, Runner, Maze, Multiplayer, Tracking Console, and Two-Camera Workspace.
  • Fixed the severe dark-blue-on-dark-green contrast defect in Maze’s setup modal, eliminated the 236 px desktop pillarbox void on Mole/Dodgeball, and fixed raw JSON parse errors in camera-choice.ts when the local vision service is offline.
  • Fixed Multiplayer’s hidden-modal enrollment error bug and replaced raw phase enum strings with readable labels.

4. Fewer Defensive Captions & Operator Precision

  • Deduplicated 5-place readiness status echoes, dropped internal milestone codes (M1/M2/M4) from player footers, and condensed verbose setup essays into scannable one-liners.
  • Placed Tracking Console’s Start camera directly under Input source (above the fold on desktop & mobile) and moved 10 secondary profiling stats into a collapsible disclosure.
  • Kept all honest safety boundaries intact: explicit camera start, no recording, synthetic vs. physical honesty, camera-release retry, and map-free Maze participant displays.

Checks Performed & Remaining Limitations

Actual Verification Run

  • pnpm contracts:check, pnpm typecheck:typescript, pnpm lint:typescript, pnpm format:check:typescript — passed.
  • pnpm test:typescript — 48 test files, 974 tests passed.
  • pnpm build:mirror (7 entries) & pnpm build:pages (5 entries) — passed.
  • Real-server Playwright browser checks (Chromium 157.0.4341.60, English, 1440×1000 / 390×844 / 320×740, zero camera starts, zero page errors): verify-ux-overhaul.mjs, verify-pages.mjs, verify-game-directory.mjs, verify-operator-navigation.mjs, plus slice checks for Runner, Maze, Console, and Rig.
  • pnpm check:repo — whitespace, Markdown links/anchors, and static HTML report checks passed.

Remaining Limitations

  • Python checks (pnpm check:python) were not run locally in this worktree because uv is not installed on PATH; no Python files were modified (CI runs the full Ubuntu/Windows/macOS Python matrix on the PR).
  • Browser verification used synthetic HTTP/WebSocket fixtures and never opened a physical USB camera or measured physical tracking accuracy, latency, or multiplayer rig capacity.
  • English is the only supported language. Physical M1/M4/M6/M7 hardware gates remain separate milestones.
